analysis.title: AMD 2027 server CPU growth moves from 70% to 100%
key_insights: Morgan Stanley keeps AMD at Equal-weight and raises its price target to $550 from $510. The new target is about 20x FY2028e Morgan Stanley ModelWare EPS of $27.58, down from a prior multiple of about 22x.

AMD server CPU units are up about 50% y/y through the first three quarters of 2026 (Intel up 4%), with server CPU revenue up about 90%. AMD guided to another year of 100%+ server CPU revenue growth in 2027, versus 70% before.

Morgan Stanley's new estimates put AMD at slightly more than 60% of the total unit growth between AMD and Intel next year. Intel loses roughly the same amount of unit share in 2027 as in 2026. The note says Intel is not materially improving the rate of share loss. Intel's earliest chance at competitive parity is the second half of 2028.

The note keeps a clear preference for AMD over Intel in server CPUs and says the fabless model is beating the integrated (IDM) model. It is cautious on extrapolating current server growth because the server CPU shortage may not last and about two-thirds of the market (Intel) is struggling to grow.

AMD recognized its first Helios revenue in the quarter. Anchor customers reported high 2027 demand and higher internal forecasts than 90 days ago. Morgan Stanley keeps a base case of about 3GW of GPU deployments next year. Its 2026 GPU estimate rises only about $500mn, and its 2027 GPU estimate moves from $38bn to $40bn.

A $1.1bn accounting charge tied to warrants lowered GAAP EPS to 43% below non-GAAP. The charge compares with about $3.5bn of GPU revenue in the quarter. Morgan Stanley says AMD's revenue per GW is close to its dilution per GW with two-thirds of its large customers. It argues this should weigh on AMD's multiple, similar to circular-financing concerns at large caps.
AMD guided Q4 revenue to a $17bn midpoint (±3%), above the Street at $16.287bn and Morgan Stanley's $16.413bn. Guided gross margin is about 55%, slightly below the Street at 55.1%.

The PC correction is in line with Intel's results. Morgan Stanley models AMD client revenue down 23% q/q in Q4, about $400mn lower than the estimate it cut going into the quarter. It models the client CPU segments troughing down in the mid-30s y/y in 2Q 2026 (as printed) and ODM PC builds already down 30% y/y in Q4. Client is under 10% of revenue.

Morgan Stanley expects GPU to be 42% of AMD's business in 2027 and 46% in 2028. The largest GPU peers trade at about 10x 2028 P/E versus AMD near 20x. The note says the multiple gap is too wide for companies it sees as having more defensible XPU positions. It also says AMD's 100% y/y server CPU growth is still unlikely to outpace ARM, and that the share and pricing power debate will get louder next year.

Morgan Stanley's FY2027 estimates rise to $98.941bn revenue, 55.6% non-GAAP gross margin and $18.77 non-GAAP EPS, from $89.13bn, 55.4% and $15.64. FY2028 estimates are $141.620bn revenue (43% growth), 56.6% gross margin and $28.49 EPS, from $126.308bn, 56.5% and $23.71. Corporate growth for 2027 is now above 80%, versus Morgan Stanley's prior 74%.

market_movers.rationale: Price target rises to $550 from $510 on higher server CPU estimates and about 20x FY2028e EPS. Rating stays Equal-weight because AMD trades at a premium to AI semiconductor peers and AI expectations are high.

Morgan Stanley prefers AMD over Intel in server CPUs because Intel is losing unit share. Its Intel valuation is about 38x CY2027 EPS of $1.98, reflecting leverage beyond 2027 and foundry optionality, despite longer-term skepticism.

sector_views.rationale: Morgan Stanley's industry view on semiconductors is Attractive. Strength in data center, led by server CPU, offsets weakness in PCs.

earnings_insights: AMD reported F3Q26 non-GAAP EPS of $2.09 against the Street at $1.95 and Morgan Stanley's estimate of $1.96. Reported on 11/4/2026 (note dated Nov 4).
AMD reported F3Q26 revenue of $13.377bn (+16.0% q/q, +44.7% y/y) against the Street at $13.096bn and Morgan Stanley's estimate of $13.132bn.
Data Center revenue was $8.546bn (+27.2% q/q, +96.9% y/y). Client was $2.949bn (-3.7% q/q, +7.2% y/y). Gaming was $0.773bn (-0.8% q/q, -40.4% y/y). Embedded was $1.109bn (+13.5% q/q, +29.4% y/y).
Reported non-GAAP gross margin was 55.9%, in line with the Street at 55.9% and Morgan Stanley's estimate of 55.9%.
Guidance for the December quarter is revenue of $17bn at the midpoint (±3%), implying 27.1% sequential growth. Guided gross margin is about 55%, down 94bps q/q and down 193bps y/y.

Morgan Stanley's Q4 2026 estimates are revenue of $17.11bn, 55.1% non-GAAP gross margin, 33.1% non-GAAP operating margin and non-GAAP EPS of $2.96. Full-year non-GAAP EPS estimates are $8.09 for 2026 (prior $7.70), $18.77 for 2027 (prior $15.64) and $28.49 for 2028 (prior $23.71).
Reported GAAP EPS was 43% below non-GAAP, driven by the $1.1bn accounting charge related to warrants.
risk_factors: Intel's server CPUs in 2027 could stifle AMD's momentum and let Intel regain share.
AMD could lose graphics share to NVIDIA, or datacenter GPU could underperform expectations.
The AI GPU business depends on one or two large customers, and AMD's revenue per GW is close to its dilution per GW with two-thirds of its large customers.
The server CPU shortage may end, and Morgan Stanley is concerned about peak cyclical conditions in CPUs.
ARM could take share or pricing power in server CPUs faster than AMD grows.

tension_points.theme: AMD server CPU share versus valuation
tension_points.bull_case: AMD server CPU units are up about 50% y/y and revenue up about 90%. 2027 guidance is for 100%+ server CPU revenue growth. Intel cannot offer competitive parity before the second half of 2028. Morgan Stanley's base case is a $550 target at about 20x FY2028e EPS.
tension_points.bear_case: The $1.1bn warrant charge shows the cost of customer deals. AMD revenue per GW is close to dilution per GW with two-thirds of its large customers. The largest GPU peers trade at about 10x 2028 P/E versus AMD near 20x. ARM may outpace AMD's server CPU growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bear case at $300 (about 17x FY2028e EPS of $18.16) if AMD loses momentum in AI and Intel regains its footing in server. Bull case at $750 if the datacenter GPU business closes the gap with Nvidia.
